title: Love made visible
hook: Gibran: work is love made visible (The Prophet, 1923)

segments.voice: Yesterday, William Morris and his three hopes. Your line was pleasure in the work itself. Which pointless task did you drop? Today, a poet who says what good work is made of. Day nine hundred six.

A ship is waiting in the harbor to take a man home after years away. Before he boards, the people of the city gather around him and, one by one, ask him to speak. About love. About marriage. About children. Later a farmer, a ploughman, steps forward and asks him to speak of work. That's a scene from The Prophet, a book by the Lebanese American poet Kahlil Gibran. The man is Almustafa, and inside his long answer about work sit five words: "Work is love made visible." Today's word is the one who said it: Almustafa.
screen: `A SHIP IN THE HARBOR.` → `A FARMER ASKS ABOUT WORK.` → `FIVE WORDS.`

segments.voice: First, the claim itself. Love, on its own, can't be seen. You can't photograph it. But a meal can be seen. A mended coat. A swept step. In Almustafa's answer, work is where love leaves the inside of a person and becomes something you can touch. Second, what working with love looks like, in paraphrase. He says it's like weaving cloth with threads drawn from your own heart, as if someone you love would wear it. Building a house as if your beloved would live in it. Sowing seeds with tenderness, as if the one you love would eat the harvest. The test is simple: who is this for, in your mind, while you make it? Third, the hard half. Almustafa doesn't only praise. He warns, again in paraphrase, that bread baked with indifference is bitter bread, and feeds only half of a person's hunger. Grudge the crushing of the grapes, he says, and the grudge becomes a poison in the wine. It's a sharp image. The same loaf, two different breads. Fourth, how this gathers up the days just before it. Ihsan asked for excellence, as though seen. Qing forgot the prize. Ruskin wanted joy in the making. Morris wanted hope in it. Gibran names what might be underneath all of them: the person you're doing it for. It doesn't have to be grand. A shirt ironed for a parent's interview. A gate fixed before a neighbor gets home. A bed made for a guest. Seen this way, an ordinary chore is a small, visible message, even if nobody ever reads it as one.
screen: `LOVE YOU CAN TOUCH.` · `AS IF THE BELOVED WOULD WEAR IT.` · `BITTER BREAD.` · `WHO IS IT FOR?` · then, large: `WORK IS LOVE MADE VISIBLE.`

segments.voice: Settle, and let the breath soften. Bring to mind someone you love. Let their face come clear. Now think of one small job you could do for them today. Folding their laundry. Fixing the thing they mentioned. Cooking the dish they like. Picture yourself doing it, slowly, with them in mind the whole time, the way Almustafa describes weaving cloth for the beloved. Let the job and the person sit together in your attention. If you pray, you can hold them in your own tradition's words. The bell holds the time.
Almustafa. The speaker in Gibran's The Prophet who tells the ploughman that work is love made visible. Today's word.
Your line: a small, visible message. Today, do one job for someone you love, and keep them in mind while you do it. Day nine hundred six.

howItsDone: Readers of The Prophet, including some people who keep a spiritual life outside any one tradition, return to its chapter on work when they think about their own work.
